title: Sunnies Run 2026 Review: An Eyewear Brand's Race Through Makati's Business Park
seo_title: Sunnies Run 2026 Review | Ayala Triangle, Makati
meta_description: Sunnies Run 2026 review: October 4 at Ayala Triangle Gardens, Makati -- a lifestyle-brand race through the Philippines' premier financial district.
dek: Set for 4 October 2026 at Ayala Triangle Gardens, this race brings eyewear and lifestyle brand Sunnies into Makati's central business district, on land that was once Manila's pre-WWII airport.
verdict: Sunnies Run brings a distinctive lifestyle/fashion-brand sponsorship to Metro Manila's most exclusive business district -- Ayala Triangle, the sub-district bounded by Ayala Avenue, Makati Avenue and Paseo de Roxas that houses the Philippines' major banks, multinationals, and corporate headquarters. The 2-hectare Ayala Triangle Gardens venue has a genuinely unusual history: the land was once Nielson Field, Manila's pre-World War II airport, decommissioned in 1948. Four distances (21.1K/10K/5K/1K) give it broad accessibility, and RunRio's organisational experience across many other events in this research batch is a reasonable proxy for what to expect logistically.

sections.heading: A Lifestyle Brand's Race in Manila's Financial Core
paragraphs: Sunnies Run is organised by RUNRIO Inc. at Ayala Triangle, Makati, offering four distances: 21.1K, 10K, 5K and 1K. [1] Sunnies is a well-known Philippine eyewear and lifestyle brand, giving this race a distinctly fashion-forward sponsorship angle compared to the sportswear, beverage and fintech brands seen elsewhere in this research batch.

sections.heading: Ayala Triangle: From Airport to Business District
paragraphs: The Ayala Triangle is a sub-district of the Makati Central Business District, bounded by Ayala Avenue, Makati Avenue and Paseo de Roxas, home to Ayala Corporation and many multinational companies, banks and other major businesses. [2] Its centrepiece, the 2-hectare Ayala Triangle Gardens, opened to the public in November 2009 -- but the land itself has a striking history: it was once the 42-hectare Nielson Field, Manila's pre-World War II airport, decommissioned in 1948 and later redeveloped into today's commercial district.

sections.heading: Four Distances for a Broad Field
paragraphs: The race spans 21.1K, 10K, 5K and 1K, giving it genuine accessibility from serious half-marathon runners down to a family-friendly 1K category -- a similar wide-spread approach to other RunRio-organised races covered in this research batch, like the EastWest Dream Run and Decathlon Run. [1]

paragraphs: As of this writing, registration status for Sunnies Run has not been announced. [1] Given the brand's consumer profile and the venue's central Makati location, demand could move quickly once sign-ups open -- worth watching official channels closely.
